standard.title: Communicating Science Effectively
standard.description: write and create texts to communicate ideas, findings and arguments effectively for identified purposes and audiences, including selection of appropriate content, language and text features, using digital tools as appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can write and create science texts with appropriate language choices for different purposes and audiences (AC9S7I08, 7-8 band). They now extend to texts that explicitly address validity and reproducibility, culturally responsive content selection, and multi-modal public communication.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students write and create texts that communicate science ideas, findings and arguments effectively — including investigation reports with validity discussion, interactive digital presentations, and public campaign texts — selecting content and language that is appropriate, accurate and culturally responsive.

nodes.label: Science texts are crafted for effective communication with specific audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select appropriate content and language features for a given science communication purpose and audience, and produce texts that communicate findings and arguments effectively — including culturally responsive content selection.
nodes.minimum_width: Students produce a science text in a given form with appropriate content, language and structure for the specified purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Students produce investigation reports including introduction (relevant theory), results (using representations), discussion (argument based on results, explanation of outliers, validity and reproducibility analysis); create interactive digital presentations; plan public communication campaigns; and select culturally responsive language and content when communicating First Nations Australians' knowledge.
wider: Write a scientific investigation report including: introductory theory, results with representations, and discussion addressing validity, reproducibility, and comparison with accepted values
Develop an interactive presentation showing feedback loops in human body systems — applying digital communication to represent dynamic biological processes
Plan a social media campaign to encourage young people to reduce their carbon footprint — applying science content to a genuine public communication purpose
Select content and language that is culturally responsive and maintains cultural protocols when communicating about First Nations Australians' knowledges

response_modes.reason: Students default to a single communication form (written report) without adapting content, language or structure to purpose and audience. Producing texts across varied forms — investigation report, interactive presentation, social media campaign — with genuinely different content selection decisions for each, builds the audience-aware communication flexibility the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The carbon footprint social media campaign provides a genuine public communication purpose that motivates careful audience and content decisions. Investigation report writing with validity discussion represents a significant step up in scientific communication sophistication.
success_criteria: Produces a science text with appropriate content, language features and structure for the specified purpose and audience
Selects culturally responsive language and content where relevant to the topic
